## Overview
Recent updates:

1. We removed 6 networks with only 1 HCW - given the bipartite and no-isolate constraints they are fixed and no variation.

2. For ergm terms present in only a subset of networks, we now restricted their evaluation in only the subset of networks. For starmix(2),  at least two such nodes should be present for the network to be included.

3. There are only 3 physicians and 1 PA/NP in all the networks, therefore it is not very meaningful to evaluate the hemophily in these two types of HCWs. We grouped physician with 'Other', and PA/NP with 'Nurse'.

4. We detected one outlier, and removed it when fitting models to speed up the convergence, and for the final model selected, we added it back in.   

# Statistical methods

We have interaction data between HCWs and residents from a sample of 100 networks. ERGMs were used to understand network structure and its associations with nodal attribues. Given the fact that only interactions can be recorded in the data, we used constriction to forbid isolates. As a result, we excluded 7 networks with only 1 HCWS, because by the definitions of bipartite + no isolates, there are no variations in these networks given the set of nodes (saturated?), leaving 93 networks. Because our data is a sample of multiple networks, the N() ergm term in package ergm.mulit{} was used to evaluate each term jointly across multiple networks. ERGM terms we examined included edges and its interaction with network size, b2start(2), b2concurrent (residents having more than 1 HCWs), gwb1dsp (geometrically weighted shared partners between HCWs), HCW type (Nurse, CNA, PT/OT/RT, Other), and resident care needs (dialysis, wound_care, bedridden, ventilator, diabetes, wheelchair, mdro). Terms are added one at a time to ensure convergence (assessed using trace plot) and reasonable goodness of fit (assessed using standardized pearson's residuals using function gofN()). For highly correlated terms (b2star, b2condurrent, gwb1dsp), we kept the one that gives the smallest AIC/BIC and dropped the rest. As the model got more complex and the algorithms were slow to converge, we removed one outlier to speed up the convergence. The largest model with all terms being significant was selected as the best model. We then used the estimated coefficients from this model as initial values to fit the model on all 93 networks, and compared results before and after adding back the outlier.

# Fitting ERGMs
In the following models, we removed network 57 due to it frequently being an outlier.
The model fitting is a lot faster when 57 is removed. We could add it back later if needed.
```{r}
#| label: prepare-data
networks1=networks[-57] # 92 networks now

dd$NetID=as.numeric(dd$NetID)
setDT(dd)
dd=dd[NetID!=57] # also remove it from the nodal attributes data frame
dd$NetID[dd$NetID>57]=dd$NetID[dd$NetID>57]-1 # re-number the networks after removing the outlier


#' Function to configure the ERGM model for the paper
#' @param dat A data frame of vertex-level attributes. It should include
#' Nurse, CNA, PTOTRT, Other, dialisis, wound_care, mdro, bedridden,
#' ventilator, wheelchair
#' @param nets A list of [network] objects.
#' @param boot Logical. Whether to return a boostrap sample or not
#' @return A list with the following three elements:
#' - `ids`: Integer vector of the selected networks.
#' - `nets`: A list of the selected networks.
#' - `filters`: A list of index vectors with the needed filtering for
#' the ERGMs
#' - `n_hcp`: Number of healthcare providers per network.
#' - `n_patients`: Number of patients per network.
#' - `facility_state`: Character vector with facilities' states. 
set_ergm <- function(
  dat,
  nets,
  boot = FALSE
  ) {

  idx <- seq_along(nets)
  if (boot) {
    # Sampling the networks
    idx <- sample(idx, replace = TRUE) |> sort()
    nets <- nets[idx]

    # Redoing indices
    dat[, .id := 1:.N, by = "NetID"]

    # Merging in
    dat_idx <- data.table(
      NetID = idx,
      NetID_new = 1:length(idx)
    )

    dat_new <- merge(
      x = dat_idx,
      y = dat,
      by = "NetID",
      all.x = TRUE,
      all.y = FALSE
    )

    setorder(dat_new, "NetID", ".id")

    # Saving the new position id
    dat_new[, NetID := NetID_new]
    dat_new[, NetID_new := NULL]
    dat_new[, .id = NULL]
    
    # Saving
    dat <- dat_new
  }

  ans <- list()

  ans$Nurse  = dat[, n:=sum(Nurse==1), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)]
  ans$CNA    = dat[, n:=sum(CNA==1), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)]
  ans$PTOTRT = dat[, n:=sum(PTOTRT==1), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)]
  ans$Other  = dat[, n:=sum(Other==1), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)] 

  # For b2factor (resident type), the networks need to have at least 1 resident of that type. 
  ans$dialysis   <- dat[, n:=sum(dialysis=='Yes'), NetID][n>0, unique(NetID)]
  ans$wound_care <- dat[, n:=sum(wound_care=='Yes'), NetID][n>0, unique(NetID)] 
  ans$mdro       <- dat[, n:=sum(mdro=='Yes'), NetID][n>0, unique(NetID)]
  ans$bedridden  <- dat[, n:=sum(bedridden=='Yes'), NetID][n>0, unique(NetID)]  

  # For b1startmix(2), at least two residents of such type need to be present in the network.
  ans$dialysis2   <- dat[, n:=sum(dialysis=='Yes'), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)]
  ans$diabetes2   <- dat[, n:=sum(diabetes=='Yes'), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)]
  ans$wound_care2 <- dat[, n:=sum(wound_care=='Yes'), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)]
  ans$ventilator2 <- dat[, n:=sum(ventilator=='Yes'), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)]
  ans$mdro2       <- dat[, n:=sum(mdro=='Yes'), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)]
  ans$wheelchair2 <- dat[, n:=sum(wheelchair=='Yes'), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)]

  n_hcp <- sapply(nets, \(net) summary(net~b1degrange(0)))
  n_patients <- sapply(nets, \(net) summary(net ~ b2degrange(0)))

  c(
    list(ids = idx, nets = nets, filters = ans),
    ans,
    list(
      n_hcp = n_hcp,
      n_patients = n_patients,
      n_tot = n_hcp + n_patients,
      facility_state = sapply(nets, \(net) unique(net %v% "state"))
    )
  )

}

model_data <- set_ergm(dat = dd, nets = networks1)
```

We will also be applying scaling based on the number of actors/entities in the network. We calculate the number of each using the following code:

Common controls for ergm models: we use Stochastic approximation since it is fast. 
```{r}
#| label: controls
default_control.1 <- list(
  seed            = 44485,
  main.method     = "Stochastic-Approximation", # Robbins-Monro Stochastic Approx.
  SA.nsubphases   = 4 * 1, # 1 the default
  SA.burnin       = 1024 * 4, # Twice the default
  SA.interval     = 1024 * 4 # four times... This is being passed to SA instead
)
```

Model 0: edges only.
Since we do not have isolates in our network by design, we restrict the network by adding offset terms b1degree(0) and b2degree(0) with coefficients -Inf.
```{r}
#| label: model0
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: hide
res0 <- with(model_data, ergm(
  Networks(nets) ~
  N(~edges, ~log(n_tot))+
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", c(default_control.1))
  ))

res0_n_tot2 <- with(model_data, ergm(
  Networks(nets) ~
  N(~edges, ~log(n_tot) + I(log(n_tot)^2))+
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", c(default_control.1))
))

# Using the other numbers
res0_n_hcp <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~log(n_hcp))+
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", c(default_control.1))
  )

res0_n_hcp2 <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~log(n_hcp) + I(log(n_hcp)^2))+
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", c(default_control.1))
)

res0_n_patients <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~log(n_patients))+
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", c(default_control.1))
  )

res0_state <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~ log(n) + I(as.factor(facility_state)))+
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", c(default_control.1))
)

res0_state_log_n2 <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~ log(n) + I(log(n)^2) + I(as.factor(facility_state)))+
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", c(default_control.1))
)

res0_state_log_n2_no_intercept <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~ -1 + log(n) + I(log(n)^2) + I(as.factor(facility_state)))+
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", c(default_control.1))
)

# Wrapper function of texreg::* to remove the
# offset terms and make the table easier to read.
tabulator <- function(x, ..., tmethod = texreg::screenreg) {

  .mapper <- function(x) {
    if (!inherits(x, "ergm") && length(x) > 1) {
      ans <- unique(unlist(sapply(x, .mapper)))
      return(
        setNames(
          as.list(ans),
          ans
        )
      )
    }

    x_coefs <- coef(x) |> names()
    x_coefs <- x_coefs[!grepl("^offset", x_coefs)]
    setNames(
      as.list(x_coefs),
      x_coefs
    )
  }

  maps <- .mapper(x)

  tmethod(
    x,
    custom.coef.map = maps,
    ...
    )

}


tabulator(
  list(
    `log(n)` = res0,
    `log(n_tot + n_tot^2)` = res0_n_tot2,
    `log(n_hcp)` = res0_n_hcp,
    `log(n_hcp + n_hcp^2)` = res0_n_hcp2,
    `log(n_patients)` = res0_n_patients,
    `+ state + log(n)` = res0_state,
    `+ log(n)^2` = res0_state_log_n2,
    `+ log(n)^2 (no intercept)` = res0_state_log_n2_no_intercept
  ),
  single.row = TRUE
)
```

[REVIEW] Adding the effect at the state level did significantly improve the model fit. Compared to California, the other states tend to have more dense networks, indicating more interactions between HCWs and residents. 

Since the log(n) scaling tries to adjust for invariance of the degree in network size, the right approach in this application is to use log(n hcp) since the degree of patients more invariant than that of HCP. As the number of patients increases, the degree of HCPs increases, but the degree of patients does not necessarily increase as much. Therefore, we will be using log(n_hcp) for the rest of the models.

Add b2 2-star (second level 2-stars) term:
```{r}

#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: hide
best_model <- res0_state

res1 <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~ log(n) + I(as.factor(facility_state)))+
  N(~b2star(2), ~log(n_hcp) + I(log(n_hcp)^2))+
  +offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", c(default_control.1))
)
```

Now try gwb1dsp - (b2star2, b2concurrent, and gwb1dsp are all correlated, counting HCWs sharing residents)
```{r} 
#| label: model2
#| cache: true
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: hide
# This takes a long time to run so we just load the saved result in the next chunk.
res2.cnew <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~ log(n) + I(as.factor(facility_state)))+
  N(~gwb1dsp(0.75, fixed=TRUE), ~log(n_hcp) + I(log(n_hcp)^2))+ # we compared decay parameter of 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1. 0.75 seems to fit the best.
  +offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", default_control.1))

res2.cnew_simpler <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~ log(n) + I(as.factor(facility_state)))+
  N(~gwb1dsp(0.75, fixed=TRUE))+ # we compared decay parameter of 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1. 0.75 seems to fit the best.
  +offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", default_control.1))
```


Model 2 fits the best. We can now compare with using an interaction with log(n)

```{r}
#| label: model2-with-log_n
# Changing the best model
best_model <- res2.cnew

res2.cnew_log_n_decay <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~ log(n) + I(as.factor(facility_state)))+
  gwb1dsp(cutoff=40) + # N(~gwb1dsp(), ~ log(n))+
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", default_control.1))

gb1dsp_decay <- coef(res2.cnew_log_n_decay)["gwb1dsp.decay"]

res2.cnew_log_n_simpler <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~ log(n) + I(as.factor(facility_state)))+
  N(~gwb1dsp(decay = gb1dsp_decay, fixed = TRUE), ~log(n_hcp) + log(n_patients)) +
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", default_control.1))

res2.cnew_log_n <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~ log(n) + I(as.factor(facility_state)))+
  N(~gwb1dsp(decay = gb1dsp_decay, fixed = TRUE), ~ log(n_hcp) + I(log(n_hcp)^2))+
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", default_control.1))

res2.cnew_log_n_75 <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~ log(n) + I(as.factor(facility_state)))+
  N(~gwb1dsp(decay = 0.75, fixed = TRUE), ~ log(n_hcp))+
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", default_control.1))

res2.cnew_log_n_simpler_state <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~ log(n) + I(as.factor(facility_state)))+
  N(~gwb1dsp(decay = gb1dsp_decay, fixed = TRUE), ~log(n_hcp) + log(n_patients) + I(as.factor(facility_state))) +
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
```

[REVIEW] Using Stewart, Schweinberger, Bojanowski, and Morris (2019) (as suggested by the reviewer), I estimated the decay parameter directly, and the used it as an input for the subsequent models. I was not able to directly estimate it with the interaction effect as ERGM failed with an error `objfun returned gradient not having all elements finite`.

```{r}
res5new_log_patients_2 <- ergm(
  Networks(networks1) ~
  N(~edges, ~ log(n) + I(as.factor(facility_state)))+
  N(~gwb1dsp(gb1dsp_decay, fixed=TRUE), ~ log(n_hcp) + log(n_patients))+
  N(~b2starmix(2, 'Nurse'), ~log(n_patients) + I(log(n_patients)^2), subset=Nurse)+ # has to be numeric
    N(~b2factor('dialysis'), subset=dialysis)+
    N(~b2factor('wound_care'), subset=wound_care)+
    N(~b2factor('bedridden'), subset=bedridden)+
  offset(b1degree(0))+offset(b2degree(0)),
  offset.coef = c(-Inf, -Inf),
  control = do.call("control.ergm", default_control.1))

tabulator(
  list(
    'Current'=best_model,
    'b2factors'=res5new_old,
    '+log(n)'=res5new_log_n,
    '+log(n) + log(n)^2'=res5new_log_n_2,
    '+log(n_patients)'=res5new_log_patients,
    '+log(n_patients) + log(n_patients)^2'=res5new_log_patients_2
  ),
  single.row = TRUE
)
```

[REVIEW] Whether to use `n_hcp` or `n_patients` is not the same all the time. Using both for the geometrically weighted dyad-wise shared partners improved overall fit. Using those terms in the b2starmix and b2factor terms did not improve the fit.

[REVIEW] Adding the PTOTRT starmix term improved the model fit, but adding the log(n) scaling did not improve the fit. So far, the new model is doing substantially better than the first version of the paper

Additional test, centering log(n) at mean(log(n)) to see if it helps with convergence.

```{r}
# Centered

log_n_hcp_centered <- log(n_hcp) - mean(log(n_hcp))
```

```{r}
# Resetting, keeping only the seed
load('data/dd_nodal_attr.RData')
dim(dd)
setDT(dd)
dd$NetID=as.numeric(dd$NetID)

Nurse  = dd[, n:=sum(Nurse==1), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)] |> as.numeric() # requiring at least 2 nurses in a network 
CNA    = dd[, n:=sum(CNA==1), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)] |> as.numeric()
PTOTRT = dd[, n:=sum(PTOTRT==1), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)] |> as.numeric()
Other  = dd[, n:=sum(Other==1), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)] 
nuni(c(Other, PTOTRT)) # 46

wh=intersect(Nurse, PTOTRT)
length(wh)
dcheck=dd[NetID %in% wh & group=='hcw', .(NetID, Nurse, PTOTRT, Other, CNA)]
dcheck[, count:=sum(CNA=="1")+sum(Other=="1"), NetID]
PTOTRT.nurse=as.numeric(dcheck[count>1, unique(NetID)])
length(PTOTRT.nurse) # all 30 networks are fine!

dialysis=dd[, n:=sum(dialysis=='Yes'), NetID][n>0, unique(NetID)]
wound_care=dd[, n:=sum(wound_care=='Yes'), NetID][n>0, unique(NetID)] 
mdro=dd[, n:=sum(mdro=='Yes'), NetID][n>0, unique(NetID)] 
bedridden=dd[, n:=sum(bedridden=='Yes'), NetID][n>0, unique(NetID)]  # requiring at least 2 nurses in a network 
bedridden

dialysis2=dd[, n:=sum(dialysis=='Yes'), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)]
diabetes2=dd[, n:=sum(diabetes=='Yes'), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)]
wound_care2=dd[, n:=sum(wound_care=='Yes'), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)] 
ventilator2=dd[, n:=sum(ventilator=='Yes'), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)] 
mdro2=dd[, n:=sum(mdro=='Yes'), NetID][n>1, unique(NetID)]

wheelchair2
```
